chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who mortgages something with his companion, and there is no proof between them regarding it. The one holding the mortgage claimed it was for a thousand, and the owner of the mortgage said, 'It is only for one hundred.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The burden of proof is upon the one holding the mortgage that it is for a thousand; and if he does not have proof, then the oath is upon the mortgagor.'
ai.seo_question: How is a dispute over the value of a mortgage resolved in Shia jurisprudence when there is no written contract?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'Al-Bayyinah 'ala al-Mudda'i' (proof is upon the claimant) in pledge disputes, specifically addressing scenarios lacking written documentation. It clarifies that the holder of the pledge bears the burden of proof for any claimed increase in value; failing that, the mortgagor's oath prevails for the lower amount, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and evidentiary standards in commercial transactions.
